cosmic-photon-emission-observation-time-.intuitive_summary: Because light travels at a finite speed through an expanding universe, looking out into deep space corresponds directly to looking back in cosmic time to earlier epochs.

temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.title: Lapse Factor of the Metric Temporal Component
temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.description: Represents the square root magnitude of the covariant temporal metric component in a mostly-plus signature, serving as the gravitational redshift and time-dilation factor for stationary observers.
temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.conceptual_definition: In general relativity using a signature with $g_{00} < 0$ (such as $(-,+,+,+)$), the expression $\sqrt{-g_{00}}$ defines the lapse function or redshift factor relating coordinate time differentials $dt$ to the differential proper time $d\tau$ elapsed along the worldline of a stationary observer via $d\tau = \sqrt{-g_{00}}\, dt$.
temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.interpretation: The component $g_{00}$ is the covariant time-time component of the metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$. For a static or stationary metric with $dx^i = 0$, the invariant line element reduces to $ds^2 = g_{00} c^2 dt^2 = -c^2 d\tau^2$, leading directly to $d\tau = \sqrt{-g_{00}}\, dt$. Thus, $\sqrt{-g_{00}}$ acts as the local conversion factor between coordinate time and physical proper time.
temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.limits_and_boundary: In flat Minkowski spacetime, $g_{00} = -1$, recovering standard time progression $\sqrt{-g_{00}} = 1$. In the weak-field Newtonian limit, $\sqrt{-g_{00}} \approx \sqrt{1 + 2\Phi/c^2} \approx 1 + \Phi/c^2$. At an event horizon or infinite redshift surface where $g_{00} \to 0$, $\sqrt{-g_{00}} \to 0$, indicating that proper time appears to freeze relative to an asymptotic observer at infinity.
temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.symmetry_origin: General covariance and diffeomorphism invariance under stationary spacetime symmetries generated by a timelike Killing vector field $\xi = \partial_t$, where $g_{00} = \xi^\mu \xi_\mu$.

g_{00}.name: Covariant temporal metric component
g_{00}.description: The time-time component of the covariant metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ in spacetime coordinates

temporal-metric-component-magnitude-6e26.intuitive_summary: It quantifies the rate at which local stationary clocks tick relative to coordinate time: the closer $g_{00}$ is to zero (such as near an event horizon), the more severe the gravitational time dilation.

ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.title: CKM Matrix Element Product $V_{cd}V_{cb}^*$
ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.description: A bilinear product of Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix elements representing the charm-quark contribution to the $b \to d$ unitarity triangle relation.
ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.conceptual_definition: The bilinear product $V_{cd}V_{cb}^*$ combines the charm-to-down transition element $V_{cd}$ with the complex conjugate of the charm-to-bottom element $V_{cb}^*$. In the Standard Model of particle physics, this quantity serves as one of the three complex vectors in the complex plane whose sum vanishes according to the orthogonality relation between the first and third columns of the CKM matrix: $V_{ud}V_{ub}^* + V_{cd}V_{cb}^* + V_{td}V_{tb}^* = 0$.
ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.interpretation: In this expression, $V_{cd}$ is the weak charged-current coupling amplitude between a charm quark $c$ and a down quark $d$, while $V_{cb}^*$ denotes the complex conjugate of the transition amplitude between a charm quark $c$ and a bottom quark $b$. In the Wolfenstein parameterization up to $\mathcal{O}(\lambda^5)$, $V_{cd} \approx -\lambda$ and $V_{cb}^* \approx A\lambda^2$, yielding a real leading-order value of $-A\lambda^3$ with vanishingly small imaginary corrections at tree level.
ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.limits_and_boundary: In the limit of vanishing quark mass hierarchies and zero mixing angles (Cabibbo angle $\theta_C \to 0$), $V_{cd} \to 0$ and $V_{cb} \to 0$, causing $V_{cd}V_{cb}^* \to 0$. In a two-generation limit, third-generation coupling vanishes identically ($V_{cb} = 0$).
ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.symmetry_origin: Originates from the global $U(3)_Q \times U(3)_u \times U(3)_d$ flavor symmetry broken down by the Yukawa sector, subject to exact $3 \times 3$ unitarity ($V_{\text{CKM}}^\dagger V_{\text{CKM}} = \mathbb{I}$) guaranteed by the $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ electroweak gauge structure.

V_{cb}^*.description: Complex conjugate of the matrix element governing the weak transition amplitude between charm and bottom quarks

ckm-matrix-element-product-vcdvcb-2fde31.intuitive_summary: In the graphical depiction of quark mixing unitarity, $V_{cd}V_{cb}^*$ forms the base-scaling side of the primary Unitarity Triangle, quantifying the intermediate charm-quark amplitude in loop-mediated flavor transitions.

joint-probability-of-two-events-84682566.title: Joint Probability of Two Events
joint-probability-of-two-events-84682566.description: The joint probability measure quantifying the likelihood of the concurrent realization of two events in a common probability space.
joint-probability-of-two-events-84682566.conceptual_definition: In Kolmogorov probability theory, given a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ and two events $A, B \in \mathcal{F}$, the joint probability $P(A \cap B)$ (often denoted $P(A \text{ and } B)$) is the probability measure assigned to the intersection of the two event subsets. By the definition of conditional probability, it satisfies the product rule $P(A \cap B) = P(A|B)P(B) = P(B|A)P(A)$, reducing to $P(A)P(B)$ if and only if the events are statistically independent.
joint-probability-of-two-events-84682566.interpretation: The expression $P(A \cap B)$ represents the probability measure of the intersection event $A \cap B \subset \Omega$. The terms $P(A)$ and $P(B)$ denote the marginal probabilities of events $A$ and $B$, respectively, while $P(A|B)$ denotes the conditional probability of $A$ given the occurrence of $B$. The value is bounded strictly by $0 \le P(A \cap B) \le \min(P(A), P(B)) \le 1$.
joint-probability-of-two-events-84682566.limits_and_boundary: When events $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive ($A \cap B = \emptyset$), $P(A \cap B) = 0$. When one event is a subset of the other ($A \subseteq B$), $P(A \cap B) = P(A)$. When $A$ and $B$ are statistically independent, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$. In the limit of certainty where $P(B) = 1$, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)$.
joint-probability-of-two-events-84682566.symmetry_origin: Permutation symmetry of the Boolean set intersection $A \cap B = B \cap A$, ensuring commutativity of the joint probability distribution.

unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.title: Unimodular Metric Condition
unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.description: The unimodular gauge condition constrains the determinant of the Lorentzian spacetime metric tensor to negative unity, ensuring that the invariant four-volume element coincides directly with the coordinate volume measure.
unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.conceptual_definition: The unimodular condition $\sqrt{-g} = 1$ is a coordinate-fixing constraint in general relativity and unimodular gravity that normalizes the volume element density. Here, $g = \det(g_{\mu\nu})$ is the determinant of the four-dimensional metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, reducing the general diffeomorphism group to transverse or volume-preserving diffeomorphisms $\mathrm{SDiff}(\mathcal{M})$.
unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.interpretation:
In this condition, $g$ represents the determinant $\det(g_{\mu
u})$ of the spacetime metric tensor $g_{\mu
u}$, and $\sqrt{-g}$ is the scalar density of weight $+1$ acting as the Jacobian volume factor. Setting $\sqrt{-g} = 1$ equates the covariant volume element $d\Omega = \sqrt{-g} \, d^4x$ to the standard coordinate differential volume $d^4x$. This constraint restricts coordinate transformations $x^\mu 	o x'^\mu$ to those satisfying $\det(\partial x'^\mu / \partial x^
u) = 1$, isolating the trace of Einstein's field equations and rendering the cosmological constant an integration constant.
unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.limits_and_boundary: In flat Minkowski spacetime with standard Cartesian coordinates $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \operatorname{diag}(-1, 1, 1, 1)$, the determinant is $g = -1$, trivially satisfying $\sqrt{-g} = 1$. In curvilinear or non-inertial systems (such as spherical coordinates where $\sqrt{-g} = r^2 \sin\theta$), this condition requires a non-standard coordinate parameterization to maintain unit volume density.
unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.symmetry_origin: Special (volume-preserving) diffeomorphism invariance $\mathrm{SDiff}(\mathcal{M})$, representing the subgroup of general coordinate transformations generated by divergence-free vector fields $\nabla_\mu \xi^\mu = 0$.

\\sqrt{-g}.description: Square root of the negative metric determinant, defining the invariant volume density

unit-spacetime-volume-element-condition-.intuitive_summary: By choosing coordinates such that the metric determinant is identically $-1$, the local stretching of spacetime coordinates is eliminated, making coordinate boxes directly reflect true physical volume.

relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.title: Relativistic Pressure Energy Constraint
relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.description: An asymptotic condition characterizing the Newtonian regime of hydrostatic equilibrium, wherein the effective work done by isotropic pressure across a spherical volume is negligibly small compared to the enclosed rest-mass energy.
relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.conceptual_definition: The condition $4\pi r^3 P \ll M c^2$ demarcates the boundary where pressure $P$ contributes negligibly to the local active gravitational mass of a spherically symmetric body of radius $r$ and enclosed mass $M$. In general relativity, pressure acts as a source of spacetime curvature through the stress-energy tensor $T^{\mu\nu}$; when this inequality is satisfied, the relativistic pressure-volume correction factor $\left(1 + \frac{4\pi r^3 P}{M c^2}\right)$ in the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation asymptotically approaches unity, recovering standard Newtonian gravity.
relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.interpretation: The parameter $P$ represents the local isotropic fluid pressure at radial coordinate $r$, while $M = M(r)$ represents the interior mass-energy enclosed within radius $r$, and $c$ is the invariant speed of light. The term $4\pi r^3 P$ scales with the total pressure-volume energy of the shell, which in strong-field gravity contributes to the effective gravitational mass $M_{\text{eff}}(r)$. When $4\pi r^3 P \ll M c^2$, this relativistic self-gravitational feedback from pressure is suppressed, ensuring that the source term in stellar structure equations is dominated strictly by matter density $\rho$.
relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.limits_and_boundary: In the Newtonian limit $c \to \infty$, $\frac{4\pi r^3 P}{M c^2} \to 0$, reducing the relativistic TOV hydrostatic balance directly to the classical equation $\frac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}r} = -\frac{G M \rho}{r^2}$. In the ultra-relativistic core collapse or neutron star limit where $P \sim \rho c^2$ and $r \sim \frac{2GM}{c^2}$, the term $\frac{4\pi r^3 P}{M c^2} \sim \mathcal{O}(1)$, triggering strong gravitational instability.
relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.symmetry_origin: Derived from general covariance and diffeomorphism invariance of general relativity in static spherically symmetric spacetimes (Schwarzschild metric), governed by local energy-momentum conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$.

relativistic-pressure-energy-constraint-.intuitive_summary: In general relativity, pressure possesses weight and gravitates just like mass-energy. This condition states that the stellar interior pressure is too small to significantly enhance its own gravitational pull.

unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.title: Zeroth-Order Taylor Expansion Term for Cosine
unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.description: The constant value $1$ serves as the zeroth-order leading term in the Maclaurin series expansion of the trigonometric cosine function $\cos\theta$. In physical systems, it establishes the asymptotic baseline value for projection factors and metric components when angular displacements vanish.
unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.conceptual_definition: The constant $1$ represents the evaluate $\cos(0) = 1$, which constitutes the foundational zeroth-order approximation in the Taylor expansion $\cos\theta = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n \theta^{2n}}{(2n)!} = 1 - \frac{\theta^2}{2} + \mathcal{O}(\theta^4)$. It corresponds to the unperturbed baseline in linearized rotational kinematics, geometric optics, and perturbation theory.
unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.interpretation: In the context of the small-angle approximation $\cos\theta \approx 1 - \frac{\theta^2}{2}$, the scalar constant $1$ defines the value of the function at the origin $\theta = 0$. For infinitesimal deviations $\theta \ll 1$, the leading-order physical behavior is governed purely by this unity baseline before quadratic curvature corrections $\mathcal{O}(\theta^2)$ become significant.
unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.limits_and_boundary: In the strict mathematical limit $\theta \to 0$, the trigonometric cosine function converges exactly to $\lim_{\theta \to 0} \cos\theta = 1$. When $\theta \gtrsim 0.1\text{ rad}$, quadratic corrections $\frac{\theta^2}{2}$ exceed a $0.5\%$ relative error threshold.
unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.symmetry_origin: Originates from the reflection symmetry of the cosine function $\cos(-\theta) = \cos(\theta)$ around $\theta = 0$, ensuring the first derivative vanishes $\left.\frac{d\cos\theta}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta=0} = 0$ and making $1$ the unique local extremum.

unity-constant-in-small-angle-approximat.intuitive_summary: For an angle approaching zero, the adjacent side of a right triangle becomes identical in length to the hypotenuse, yielding an exact ratio of one.

unidirectional-current-density-vector-6b.title: Unidirectional Inhomogeneous Current Density Vector
unidirectional-current-density-vector-6b.description: Represents a steady current density vector oriented strictly along the z-axis with spatial variation confined entirely to the x-coordinate.
unidirectional-current-density-vector-6b.conceptual_definition: The unidirectional current density vector $\boldsymbol{J} = (0, 0, J_z(x))$ describes a continuous electric current flow restricted to the $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ direction, exhibiting translational invariance along both the $y$ and $z$ Cartesian axes. Under steady-state magnetostatics, it serves as a planar source distribution generating a vector potential $\mathbf{A} = (0, 0, A_z(x))$ satisfying $\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{J} = 0$.
unidirectional-current-density-vector-6b.interpretation: The vector $\boldsymbol{J}$ is the three-dimensional electric current density measured in $\mathrm{A\cdot m^{-2}}$. Its transverse components identically vanish, $J_x = 0$ and $J_y = 0$, while the longitudinal component $J_z(x)$ is a function purely of the transverse position $x$. Because $\partial_z J_z(x) = 0$, the continuity equation $\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{J} = 0$ is trivially fulfilled for stationary charge distributions.
unidirectional-current-density-vector-6b.limits_and_boundary: In the limit $x \to \pm\infty$, physical current distributions require $J_z(x) \to 0$ rapidly enough for the total integrated current per unit width $\int_{-\infty}^\infty J_z(x) \, dx$ to remain finite.
unidirectional-current-density-vector-6b.symmetry_origin: Continuous spatial translation symmetry along the $y$ and $z$ directions, combined with global $U(1)$ electric charge conservation yielding a divergence-free current field.

net-external-force-is-zero-176d1bfb.title: Condition of Zero Net External Force
net-external-force-is-zero-176d1bfb.description: States that the vector sum of all external forces acting on a many-particle or continuum system vanishes, establishing the condition for translational equilibrium and linear momentum conservation.
net-external-force-is-zero-176d1bfb.conceptual_definition: For an $N$-particle or continuum system, the net external force $\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext, net}} = \sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf{F}_i^{\text{ext}}$ is set to zero ($\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext, net}} = \mathbf{0}$). Through Newton's second law for a system of particles, $\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\mathbf{P}_{\text{total}}}{dt}$, this condition ensures that the time derivative of the total linear momentum vanishes: $\dot{\mathbf{P}}_{\text{total}} = \mathbf{0}$.
net-external-force-is-zero-176d1bfb.interpretation: The quantity $\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext, net}}$ denotes the resultant vector sum of all forces originating from outside the chosen boundary of the system. Setting $\mathbf{F}_{\text{ext, net}} = \mathbf{0}$ implies that internal interactions (which cancel in pairs due to Newton's third law) cannot change the total momentum $\mathbf{P}_{\text{total}}$, keeping the center of mass velocity $\mathbf{v}_{\text{cm}}$ constant in an inertial reference frame.
net-external-force-is-zero-176d1bfb.limits_and_boundary: In the presence of non-inertial reference frames, fictitious inertial forces must be accounted for unless frame acceleration vanishes ($\mathbf{a}_{\text{frame}} \to \mathbf{0}$). In relativistic dynamics, the spatial force condition generalizes to the vanishing of net external four-force $\mathbf{K}_{\text{ext}}^\mu = 0$.
net-external-force-is-zero-176d1bfb.symmetry_origin: Spatial translation invariance via Noether's theorem; an isolated system with no external potential exhibits invariance under global spatial translations $\mathbf{r} \to \mathbf{r} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$, guaranteeing conservation of total linear momentum.

wavefunction-overlap-product-58f358a1.title: Wavefunction Overlap Product
wavefunction-overlap-product-58f358a1.description: The pointwise product of the complex conjugate of a quantum state wavefunction and another state wavefunction, representing the local integrand for state overlaps and transition matrix elements.
wavefunction-overlap-product-58f358a1.conceptual_definition: The wavefunction overlap product $\psi_m^* \psi_n$ forms the differential volume integrand of the Hilbert space inner product $\langle \psi_m | \psi_n \rangle = \int \psi_m^*(\mathbf{r}) \psi_n(\mathbf{r}) \, d^3r$. For $m = n$, it reduces to the spatial probability density $\rho(\mathbf{r}) = |\psi_n(\mathbf{r})|^2$, whereas for $m \neq n$, it characterizes local interference and spatial co-localization of distinct quantum states.
wavefunction-overlap-product-58f358a1.interpretation: In this expression, $\psi_m^*$ is the complex conjugate of the eigenstate or state wavefunction $\psi_m$, and $\psi_n$ is the state wavefunction for mode $n$. When $m = n$, the product $\psi_n^* \psi_n = |\psi_n|^2$ represents the Born probability density. When $m \neq n$, its integral over configuration space vanishes for mutually orthogonal states in a Hermitian basis.
wavefunction-overlap-product-58f358a1.limits_and_boundary: In the limit of non-overlapping spatial supports where $\text{supp}(\psi_m) \cap \text{supp}(\psi_n) = \emptyset$, the product $\psi_m^* \psi_n = 0$ everywhere in space. When $m = n$, the product is strictly non-negative and real: $\psi_n^* \psi_n \ge 0$.

mirror-symmetry-hodge-number-duality-38d.title: Mirror Symmetry Hodge Number Duality
mirror-symmetry-hodge-number-duality-38d.description: Relates the dimension of the Kähler moduli space of a Calabi-Yau threefold to the dimension of the complex structure moduli space of its mirror partner.
mirror-symmetry-hodge-number-duality-38d.conceptual_definition: In topological string theory and mirror symmetry, compactification of Type IIA string theory on a Calabi-Yau threefold $M$ is physically equivalent to Type IIB string theory compactified on its mirror threefold $W$. Geometrically, this requires an exchange of the Hodge diamond along its diagonal, specifically identifying the Hodge numbers $h^{1,1}(M) = h^{2,1}(W)$ and $h^{2,1}(M) = h^{1,1}(W)$, establishing an isomorphism between the Kähler moduli space $\mathcal{M}_K(M)$ and the complex structure moduli space $\mathcal{M}_C(W)$.
mirror-symmetry-hodge-number-duality-38d.interpretation: The Hodge number $h^{1,1}(M)$ measures the complex dimension of the Kähler deformation space (geometric sizes and 2-cycles) of the manifold $M$. The Hodge number $h^{2,1}(W)$ measures the complex dimension of the complex structure deformation space (shapes and 3-cycles) of the mirror manifold $W$. The equality $h^{1,1}(M) = h^{2,1}(W)$ reflects the physical duality exchanging the vector multiplet and hypermultiplet moduli spaces between Type IIA and Type IIB superstring compactifications.
mirror-symmetry-hodge-number-duality-38d.limits_and_boundary: In the large complex structure limit of $W$, quantum worldsheet instanton corrections to the Kähler potential of $M$ map to classical Picard-Fuchs differential equations governing the period integrals on $W$. cosmic-ray-spallation-nuclide-abundance-.title: Cosmic Ray Spallation Nuclide Abundance
cosmic-ray-spallation-nuclide-abundance-.description: Calculates the accumulated volumetric number density of a stable light nuclide generated through cosmic ray spallation in the interstellar medium under a constant flux and thin-target approximation.
cosmic-ray-spallation-nuclide-abundance-.conceptual_definition: The cosmic ray spallation nuclide abundance formula $n_i = F_{\text{cr}} \sigma_i n_H \tau$ determines the volumetric number density $n_i$ of a secondary isotope produced via the fragmentation of heavier target or projectile nuclei. It integrates the reaction rate per unit volume, given by the product of the incoming cosmic ray flux $F_{\text{cr}}$, the effective spallation cross-section $\sigma_i$, and the target hydrogen density $n_H$, over an effective confinement or exposure timescale $\tau$.
cosmic-ray-spallation-nuclide-abundance-.interpretation: The symbol $n_i$ represents the resulting number density of nuclide $i$. The parameter $F_{\text{cr}}$ denotes the integrated omnidirectional flux of high-energy cosmic rays traversing the interstellar medium. The quantity $\sigma_i$ is the energy-averaged production cross-section for creating nuclide $i$ via spallation. The term $n_H$ represents the number density of target nuclei (predominantly interstellar hydrogen and helium), and $\tau$ is the effective galactic residence time or exposure epoch over which spallation accumulates without significant secondary destruction or escape.
cosmic-ray-spallation-nuclide-abundance-.limits_and_boundary: In the limit $\tau \to 0$ or $F_{\text{cr}} \to 0$, the synthesized nuclide abundance vanishes ($n_i \to 0$). For large exposure times $\tau \to \infty$ or high column densities, the linear approximation breaks down, requiring a full differential transport equation with destruction cross-sections and radioactive decay terms.
cosmic-ray-spallation-nuclide-abundance-.symmetry_origin: Rooted in baryon number conservation and energy-momentum conservation across individual inelastic nuclear hadron-hadron collisions.

magnetization-and-magnetic-field-strengt.title: Magnetization and Magnetic Field Strength in Linear Media
magnetization-and-magnetic-field-strengt.description: Defines the macroscopic magnetization induced in a linear and isotropic magnetic medium as proportional to the auxiliary magnetic field strength via the dimensionless magnetic susceptibility.
magnetization-and-magnetic-field-strengt.conceptual_definition: In linear, isotropic, and homogeneous magnetic materials, the volume magnetization density $M$ arises as a direct linear response to an applied auxiliary magnetic field $H$, parameterized by the magnetic susceptibility $\chi_m$ through the scalar constitutive relation $M = \chi_m H$.
magnetization-and-magnetic-field-strengt.interpretation: The variable $M$ represents the magnitude of the magnetization vector (magnetic dipole moment per unit volume) in $\text{A}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}$, $H$ is the auxiliary magnetic field strength in $\text{A}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}$, and $\chi_m$ is the dimensionless volumetric magnetic susceptibility. For diamagnetic materials, $\chi_m < 0$ (opposing the applied field), whereas for paramagnetic materials, $\chi_m > 0$ (aligning with the applied field). In nonlinear or ferromagnetic materials, this linear relation fails due to hysteresis and saturation.
magnetization-and-magnetic-field-strengt.limits_and_boundary: In the weak-field limit ($H \to 0$), the linear approximation $M \approx \chi_m H$ is exact. In strong fields ($H \gg H_{\text{sat}}$), materials exhibit magnetic saturation ($M \to M_{\text{sat}}$), causing $\chi_m$ to become field-dependent. In a vacuum, $\chi_m = 0$, yielding $M = 0$.
magnetization-and-magnetic-field-strengt.symmetry_origin: Originates from the leading-order Taylor expansion of the macroscopic response tensor under spatial rotational invariance (isotropy) and time-reversal symmetry in the weak-field limit.
